- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +1.00 or above) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (e.g., -1.96 or below) — model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in the opposite direction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price decline — model delays recognizing downward trends, especially after sentiment shifts to negative.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model tends to overproject upward momentum; when sentiment turns negative, model underreacts and fails to anticipate sharp drops.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs as sustainable — model often assumes continuation, ignoring mean reversion or policy-driven corrections.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.35–0.40), model tends to err on the side of overoptimism — forecast too high.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high, model should not overreact; if sentiment is low, model should not underreact — apply smoothing or dampening to sentiment-driven forecasts.
